extracted.intended_audience: general readers of 19th-century biography/history (readers interested in Frederick Wilhelm I and Prussian governance)
extracted.subtask_description: A chapter-length biographical/historical essay describing Friedrich Wilhelm I's character, habits, reforms, and methods of government, emphasizing thrift, discipline, and practical reforms. The text is a literary-historical treatment rather than a procedural manual.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economy and thrift in administration
rubrics_metrics.description: He reduced his Household accordingly, at once, to the lowest footing of the indispensable; and discharged a whole regiment of superfluous official persons... Reduced to below the fifth of what it was; 55,000 THALERS, instead of 276,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prune all superfluous posts and expenses; repeatedly review lists of expenditures (the King went over his Papers three times) to find the 'effective minimum.' Examples: cutting number of lackeys/pages/horses, reducing pension lists by three-fourths, saving even small amounts (half a thaler). Scoring note: success measured by concrete reduced expenditures and elimination of idle positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needful work must be rigorously well done; needless work removed
rubrics_metrics.description: Needful work is to be rigorously well done; needless work, and ineffectual or imaginary workers, to be rigorously pitched out of doors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize essential tasks and enforce execution quality; identify and remove functions/persons that do not produce real value. Anti-pattern: tolerating 'imaginary' workers whose cost yields no real output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hatred of 'wind and humbug' — preference for realities
rubrics_metrics.description: Dire hatred of empty bladders, unrealities and hypocritical forms and pretences, what he calls 'wind and blauer dunst' (wind and blue vapor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value concrete, demonstrable results over appearances, ceremony, or rhetorical flourish. Examples: opposing courtly scandal-talk, French sumptuosity, perukes and pomp. Anti-pattern: privileging etiquette and display over substantive outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eliminate mendacity, corruption, and peculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of mendacity expunged... Mendacity not of tongue; but the far feller sort, of hand, and of heart, and of head... prevaricators, defalcators, imaginary workers, and slippery unjust persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect and remove embezzlement, corruption, and deceptive practices in administration; ensure that resources actually serve their purposes (e.g., horses actually fed and used, not pocketed by knavish stallmeister). Example: replacing 'imaginary quadrupeds' with a real, useful stable of thirty horses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce daylight to the bottom of every business (transparency & efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: He insisted on having daylight introduced to the very bottom of every business, fair-and-square observed as the rule of it, and the shortest road adopted for doing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make processes transparent, simplify administrative structures, and adopt the shortest effective procedures. Example: harmonizing conflicting boards into one GENERAL DIRECTORY to eliminate overlapping, half-done work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural and fiscal reform to prevent waste
rubrics_metrics.description: How he introduced a new mode of farming his Domain Lands... which shall be farmed on regular lease henceforth, and not wasted in peculation and indolent mismanagement as heretofore; new modes of levying his taxes and revenues of every kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reform revenue-generating institutions to lease or systematize management, tighten tax collection methods, and close avenues for mismanagement. Success metric: reduced leakage and improved returns from domains and taxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frugality, diligence, punctuality, veracity as national virtues
rubrics_metrics.description: Yearly he made his country richer; and this not in money alone... but in frugality, diligence, punctuality, veracity,--the grand fountains from which money, and all real values and valors spring for men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote cultural virtues (frugality, diligence, punctuality, truthfulness) as foundations for long-term national prosperity. Anti-pattern: short-term displays of wealth that undermine these virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persist in just reforms despite opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: If your plan is just, and a bit of Nature's plan, persist in it like a law of Nature. This secret too was known to Friedrich Wilhelm... In the space of ten years, by actual human strength loyally spent, he had managed many things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat just policies as natural laws to be patiently and stubbornly enforced; expect local resistance (example: the Magdeburg knights) and plan for sustained effort over years rather than quick fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drill the nation — maintain and improve military readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: To augment the quantity, to improve the quality... here lay the keystone... he will have an army of from seventy to a hundred thousand... the great Drill-sergeant of the Prussian Nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in training, recruitment and discipline to create a capable standing force; extend the principle of 'drilling' into civic life so the nation is habitually orderly and ready. Metric: numbers trained and quality of drills; cultural impact beyond military.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplicity of habits and scrupulous cleanliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing could exceed his Majesty's simplicity of habitudes. But one loves especially in him his scrupulous attention to cleanliness of person and of environment. He washed like a very Mussulman, five times a day... will not suffer a floor-carpet... insists on having all of wood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt austere, simple personal and institutional habits; remove unnecessary comforts that impede cleanliness or efficiency. Example: choosing wooden furniture over carpets to facilitate cleanliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality over fashion and ceremony
rubrics_metrics.description: This King did not love the French, or their fashions, at all... The Peruke, and, as it were, all that the Peruke symbolized... taxed wigs; Wig-inspectors plucking off men's periwigs to see if the government-stamp were there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize native, functional practices over imported fashions and ceremonious displays. Use regulation and even public sanction to discourage frivolous or costly fashions that signify waste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spend only when the occasion merits it
rubrics_metrics.description: The flunky world... But it is not so; intrinsically, in the main, his procedure is to be defined as honorable thrift,--verging towards avarice here and there; He can be magnificent enough too, and grudges no expense, when the occasion seems worthy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise selective generosity: avoid routine extravagance but allocate resources liberally for truly worthy or unavoidable occasions. Anti-pattern: indiscriminate splurging for vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership by doing rather than rhetorical eloquence
rubrics_metrics.description: He must DO a thing, leave it undemonstrated; once done, it will itself tell what kind of thing it is, by and by.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value action and demonstrable accomplishment over speeches and polished argument; let results validate policy. Anti-pattern: reliance on rhetoric without implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of symbolic acts/mockery to enforce norms
rubrics_metrics.description: Friedrich Wilhelm has a dumb rough wit and mockery... Dressed up his Scavenger-Executioner people... in enormous exaggeration of that costume... they solemnly crossed Count Rothenburg's field of vision... Awakening salutary reflections in him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ theatrical or symbolic public acts to shame pretension and enforce cultural norms (example: parading exaggeratedly dressed scavengers to ridicule flamboyant fashions). Use carefully to avoid counterproductive humiliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct interrogation and demand for candor
rubrics_metrics.description: He would ask in an alarming manner, 'Who are you?' ... 'Er blicke mich gerade an, Look me in the face, then!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaders should test interlocutors directly for honesty; insistence on eye contact and straightforward answers helps detect evasions. Anti-pattern: tolerating evasive or indirect replies.
